pure-announcement.rationale: This is a tutorial explaining an architectural pattern with runnable examples, not a product launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concept, MCP stateless protocol core, covers protocol-level statelessness in MCP, not the agent-memory-residence tradeoff this note centres on, so a reader still learns something new.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The tradeoffs are demonstrated with runnable code and rest on standard distributed-systems reasoning any reader can verify.

durability.rationale: The core tradeoff — client-held vs server-held conversation state and its consequences for horizontal scaling, token growth, and async workflows — is a classic architecture pattern that will hold in twelve months, while the Groq free-tier and model-name details are incidental illustration.

actionability.rationale: It gives a concrete, product-agnostic decision rule — stateless for single-turn task pipelines, stateful (with a persistent store and centralized cache to avoid localized amnesia) for long-running multi-turn assistants — that directly shapes a deployment design.

atomicity.rationale: The note carries exactly one idea, the state-residence tradeoff, and both code examples are illustrations of that same idea rather than separable concepts.
